label: after
takeaway_default: Release 100 GtC in 2050 and 50% of it is still in the air a century later; 41% after 250 years. Unlike other greenhouse gases (methane, nitrous oxide), which are chemically or photochemically destroyed, emitted carbon is not destroyed; it just moves between sinks. The result of this is that a share of carbon emissions is effectively permanent on a human timescale.
